title: Latency-tiered region routing with p50/p95 thresholds & health scoring
creator: Jae Park
description: Implement region selection logic that uses real-time latency telemetry (p50/p95) and a composite network health score to route requests across regions and customer tiers. This ticket designs, implements, tests, and rolls out a deterministic scoring function plus config-driven thresholds and fallbacks to compatible model variants when regions exceed latency or health thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Router exposes region_health_score per region in /internal/region-health API (JSON) with p50/p95, packet_loss, and composite_score
Routing decision engine can be configured by policy: prefer_low_latency | prefer_cost | balanced; default is balanced
Policies support tier overrides (gold/silver/bronze) that change p50/p95 thresholds and timeout budgets
If composite_score > fail_threshold or p95 > p95_threshold, router marks region as degraded and routes to next-best region or to fallback model variant
Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 24h, then 25% for 48h, then global if no regressions; rollback hooks available
Dashboards show health score time series and routing decision breakdown; alerts for >3 regions degraded simultaneously
Automated integration tests simulate synthetic latency/packet loss and validate routing outcomes per policy
Documentation and operator runbook covering tuning parameters and emergency cutover steps
design_notes: Core idea: derive a single composite health score per region computed every 30s from telemetry windows. Candidate formula used in prototype: composite_score = 0.6 * normalized_p95 + 0.3 * normalized_p50 + 0.1 * packet_loss_rate_normalized
Normalization: p50/p95 normalized against region-specific baselines (rolling 7d median) to avoid global bias when absolute latencies differ by region
Windowing: compute p50 over 1m and p95 over 5m windows; also compute 1h aggregates for trend detection and hysteresis
Tiering: gold tier gets tighter thresholds (p95_threshold = 120ms), silver = 250ms, bronze = 450ms. Thresholds are configurable per customer and route through Console

Fallbacks: router supports fallbacks in order: same-region compatible model variant (lower-capacity or quantized), then next-best-region, then degraded-mode response (shortened max tokens or cached prefix), finally error if none available

Config surface: routing_policy object in tenant config: {type: string, p95_threshold_ms: int, fail_threshold: float, fallback_sequence: list of strings}. Implement as top-level JSON in config store for easy experimentation
Safety: apply rate-limiting on automatic region failover to avoid mass migrations during noisy spikes; migrate at bounded QPS per-second to new region
Observability: emit decision_reason tag on every routed request with values: healthy|prefer_low_latency|tier_override|region_degraded|fallback_model
Tradeoffs: using p95 favors tail reduction but may cause more churn in routing decisions; we add hysteresis (min_duration 60s) to avoid flapping
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flags behind internal flag 'region_latency_routing_v2' and 'health_score_routing'
Phase 1: Instrumentation only — start emitting composite_score metrics and dashboard time series for 48 hours (no routing changes)
Phase 2: Simulated planner — run routing decisions in dry-run mode and collect discrepancies versus current router for 72 hours
Phase 3: Canary — 5% tenant traffic (low-risk tenants) for 24h with real routing decisions; monitor errors, latency, cost; abort if error rate > 0.5% or tail latency regressions
Phase 4: Gradual ramp — 25% for 48h, 60% for 24h, then full rollout if stable
Rollback: immediate feature-flag toggle; automated rollback if alert conditions triggered (see SLOs section)
tests: Unit tests for scoring normalization, windowing, and hysteresis logic
Integration tests: inject synthetic telemetry streams for p50/p95/packet_loss and assert routing outcomes per policy
Chaos test: inject region-wide 30% packet loss and verify fallback sequence and bounded migration rate
Performance: benchmark decision latency in router hot path must be <1ms additional median overhead
End-to-end: canary tenants validate correctness; comparison job to ensure token-level latency not regressed >5% for gold tier
metrics_and_slos: Emit per-region: telemetry.p50_ms, telemetry.p95_ms, telemetry.packet_loss, telemetry.composite_score
Alerts: composite_score > 0.8 for >2 minutes => operational alert; >0.95 for >30s => P0 escalation
Customer SLOs: gold tier p95 served region < configured threshold 99.9% of requests over 24h window
Cost monitoring: track cross-region egress increase after routing changes and alert if 24h cost delta > 15%
dependencies: ENG-9012 (Router v2 refactor) must land to expose decision hooks
ENG-8883 (Telemetry pipeline: p95/p50 aggregation) for 1m and 5m windows
PM-412 (Console policy editor) for making thresholds editable per tenant
SRE-77 (Alerting runbooks) needs update for composite_score alerts
open_questions: Should composite_score incorporate GPU saturation or queue depth metrics in addition to network latency? (pro: more holistic, con: increases noise)
What is the right decay factor for rolling baseline normalization (7d vs 14d)?
Operator UX: expose raw telemetry alongside normalized scores so operators can tune without guessing
Do we need per-model heuristics (decoder-only models vs encoder) because generation token rates impact p95 differently?
implementation_notes: Telemetry ingestion: extend collector to tag region and route, compute bucketed histograms (p50/p95), and write to metrics store every 30s
Router changes: accept metrics snapshot in decision input; add pluggable scoring function with deterministic weights (configurable by feature flag)
Backwards compatibility: keep existing weight-based region routing; new logic will be additive and behind flags
Docs/Runbook: add section 'Managing region health scores' to internal ops wiki and link in console
